newsitem.title: USA: Diller says TV ratings system should be scrapped.
newsitem.headline: Diller says TV ratings system should be scrapped.

text.p: Media mogul Barry Diller said Friday the television industry's programme-ratings system "makes no sense" and should be scrapped.
"It does not work," he told reporters after a speech at the National Press Club.

Diller, credited with launching the Fox TV network and building QVC into a home-shopping sensation, said earlier in his speech that the sheer volume of programmes made it tough to rate shows properly.
He also cited recent studies suggesting that age-restrictive advisory labels actually lure young viewers to racy programmes.

The age-based ratings -- which include TV-PG for parental guidance suggested and TV-M for mature audiences -- are to be used in conjunction with a "V-chip" that will allow parents to screen out shows they consider unsuitable for their children.

"The industry has delivered its voluntary age-based ratings system, which of course makes no sense, and consumer groups have offered their own content-based alternative, which of course also makes no sense," said Diller, now chairman of HSN Inc., the St. Petersburg, Fla.-based parent company of Home Shopping Network and Silver King Broadcasting.
Diller blamed industry executives for being too hasty to respond to political pressure and developing a ratings system they knew would be unworkable.

As an alternative, Diller said he favoured an "E-chip," or "enable chip," that would permit only G-rated family viewing. "If the point were to baby sit only when parents are away, this is the conservative baby-sitter," Diller said.
